cells.tense: Right now you are holding this without forcing it toward an answer.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Next time someone you love is in something hard, stay in it with them and don't solve it. Ten minutes beside them is plenty.
cells.core:
You can carry weight and keep it from pressing down on anything else. A thing is still undecided, and you don't shove it into a shape to feel better — you keep standing there, and that turns out to be what holding looks like when it works. Under something unformed, you stay put, and staying doesn't take your footing from under you. Whoever is nearby picks that up. Some of them soften because of it.

There is something new in your life that has not declared itself. Stay with it the way you would sit with a person in a hard week: no fixing, no deciding what it is. Give it attention for seven days and keep the question open. You may feel a pull to call it by a name before it is ready. Notice the pull. Nothing has to follow from noticing.
cells.sheetLine: You can carry what's unformed without forcing it into shape.
cells.verb: bearing what must be borne without breaking or hardening

cells.tense: Soon a future you cannot see will arrive and you are already bracing for it.
cells.act: give back what is owed, and take what is yours
cells.ask: This week, answer the help or invitation you left sitting and give one thing back in return. Then stop counting.
cells.core:
You are gripping some untried thing hard enough that it cannot move. You are bracing for a load before it has arrived, and what was strength sets into something the thing itself can feel. It's striking how much pressure you can put on something that isn't heavy yet. Nothing about next year gets clearer from a tighter grip; it just gets smaller. The grip is doing work, but not the work you want.

Something was offered to you and left untouched. Take it this week — the help, the invitation, the hand held out — and give one thing back in return, without a tally. One exchange gets the current moving both ways. You do not have to settle the whole future to make it.
cells.sheetLine: Bracing for a weight that hasn't arrived is its own weight.

cells.tense: You once stood at a door carrying something and set it down before you went through.
cells.act: stop holding what no longer serves
cells.ask: The duty that already ended is still on you. Put it down this afternoon — somewhere real, a drawer or a shelf — and don't pick it back up before evening.
cells.core:
Holding has stopped being something you do. A new thing is nearby and it hasn't been picked up at all — not because it isn't worth it, but because reaching for it now looks like the last reach did. The seed is there. You haven't put it in ground. That happens after a weight lands wrong, and it doesn't mean the ability is gone. It means the last one sat heavy and you stopped reaching for the next.

Start smaller. Some duty you finished still has your arms full — a responsibility held past its finish, something that now holds you back more than it holds anything up. Set it somewhere real this afternoon and go through to evening without picking it back up.

cells.tense: The door you are holding open was opened by your own hand, and you don't remember it.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: Ask yourself which thing you'd hate most to lose and haven't yet picked. Then take one step toward it this week — a footfall, no more.
cells.core:
You are bearing more than you notice, and standing under it keeps several things upright. You would probably call it luck, or circumstance, or not your doing. You have kept them steady a while and not put your own name on the steadying. Somebody who relies on it can feel that it holds, even when you can't tell. That is the part that stays out of sight.

There is something you might actually want, and you have not let yourself want it plainly. Pick that out — not the reasonable choice, the one you would hate to lose — and take one step the size of a footfall toward it this week. No plan past that step. Face it and move.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: 'the things in your care don't' file you under circumstance, and in Too Little that holding has already collapsed under a weight the record does not name. A reader could reasonably say the balance has no outward witnesses, or that this seat is unborn possibility rather than a load that broke them. The asks all survive being wrong — watering, treating-as-is, accepting a hand offered, turning toward what draws — they teach something even if the read misses. The sentence that serves me more than them: any line making the unrecognized strength sound like a compliment, and any 'some things are meant to be set down', which is a poster talking.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: in Too Little, that a weight landed wrong and that the last reach is why the person stopped reaching — the record says where they stand, not why, and I've kept that out of the core this time. In Unacknowledged, that somebody relies on what they hold; the record cannot know who leans, so I say it as what stays out of their own sight rather than a fact about a bystander. The asks survive a wrong read: sitting with a person in something hard, answering an open offer, setting down a finished duty, steering a step toward what draws — each teaches something even if the map missed. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that makes the not-seeing sound like a virtue waiting to be claimed.
